ambiguities.evidence: Equation T1-E3 writes a minimum over epsilon while the perturbations occur as implicitly quantified conforming objects.
ambiguities.impact: A formalization must make the existential quantification and conforming real dimensions explicit; it should not replace the common epsilon by independently minimized perturbation levels.
ambiguities.issue: The display does not explicitly bind DeltaA, Deltab, their domains, or epsilon >= 0 inside the set-builder notation. [T1-E3]

contract_plain_english: For any computed candidate x_hat for the nonsingular real system Ax = b, the smallest common relative size of simultaneous Frobenius-norm perturbations to A and 2-norm perturbations to b that makes x_hat exact is precisely the 2-norm residual divided by ||A||_F||x_hat||_2 + ||b||_2. [T1-E1, T1-E3, T1-E4]

source_evidence.observation: The standing problem is Ax = b with A in R^(n x n) nonsingular and 0 != b in R^n; x denotes its exact solution.
The paper uses the standard floating-point model, fl(.) for a computed expression, and hats for computed quantities.

For a computed solution x_hat, the paper defines the minimum common relative perturbation epsilon by (A + DeltaA)x_hat = b + Deltab, ||DeltaA||_F <= epsilon||A||_F, and ||Deltab||_2 <= epsilon||b||_2, and states that this minimum equals ||b - Ax_hat||_2/(||A||_F||x_hat||_2 + ||b||_2).

source_evidence.anchor: T1-E4: norm conventions and final sentence of Section 2
source_evidence.observation: Vector residuals use the 2-norm, matrix perturbations use the Frobenius norm, and the unqualified phrase 'backward error' subsequently means this normwise backward error.

statement.algorithm_linkage: The identity is an algorithm-independent definition for a computed solution of (1.1); it does not require a particular GMRES variant or iteration index. [T1-E1, T1-E3]
binders: A in R^(n x n) is nonsingular, 0 != b in R^n, and x solves Ax = b. [T1-E1]
x_hat is a computed solution candidate; DeltaA and Deltab have the conforming matrix and vector dimensions, and epsilon is the common relative perturbation level. [T1-E2, T1-E3]
conclusions: min{epsilon : (A + DeltaA)x_hat = b + Deltab, ||DeltaA||_F <= epsilon||A||_F, ||Deltab||_2 <= epsilon||b||_2} = ||b - Ax_hat||_2/(||A||_F||x_hat||_2 + ||b||_2). [T1-E3]
Thus the normalized residual is exactly the simultaneous normwise backward error, not merely an upper bound. [T1-E3]
constants_and_indexing: There is one shared perturbation level epsilon; separate matrix and right-hand-side tolerances are not introduced. [T1-E3]
No iteration index or dimension-dependent generic constant appears in this identity. [T1-E3]
definitions_and_conventions: A hat marks a computed quantity, whereas x without a hat is the exact solution of Ax = b. [T1-E1, T1-E2]
After this definition, 'backward error' means 'normwise backward error' unless qualified otherwise. [T1-E4]
error_notions: The backward error permits simultaneous perturbations of both A and b, controlled by one relative tolerance epsilon. [T1-E3]
The right-hand side is the true residual norm ||b - Ax_hat||_2 normalized by ||A||_F||x_hat||_2 + ||b||_2. [T1-E3]
exceptional_values: The standing assumption b != 0 makes the denominator strictly positive; this follows from (1.1) and the denominator in the definition. [T1-E1, T1-E3]
The paper does not discuss NaNs, infinities, overflow, underflow, or subnormal behavior in this definition. [T1-E2, T1-E3]
higher_order_terms: No higher-order or big-O terms are omitted in the displayed identity. [T1-E3]
hypotheses: The admissible perturbations satisfy (A + DeltaA)x_hat = b + Deltab. [T1-E3]
The same epsilon bounds both perturbations: ||DeltaA||_F <= epsilon||A||_F and ||Deltab||_2 <= epsilon||b||_2. [T1-E3]
implicit_context: The linear system is the nonsingular square real system (1.1), with nonzero right-hand side. [T1-E1]
norms: DeltaA and A are measured in the Frobenius norm. [T1-E3, T1-E4]
Deltab, b, x_hat, and b - Ax_hat are measured in the vector 2-norm. [T1-E3, T1-E4]
numerical_model: The surrounding section adopts the standard floating-point model and hat notation, but the perturbation-to-residual identity itself is an exact mathematical equality and contains no unit-roundoff parameter. [T1-E2, T1-E3]

undebatable_constraints: The perturbation equation must have the signs (A + DeltaA)x_hat = b + Deltab. [T1-E3]
The matrix norm is Frobenius and the vector norms are 2-norms. [T1-E3, T1-E4]
The claim is an equality with a minimum simultaneous perturbation, not an asymptotic estimate. [T1-E3]
